title: Towards Fully Automated Molecular Simulations: Multi-Agent Framework for Simulation Setup and Force Field Extraction
experiments_summary: Two main evaluation experiments were conducted. First, the experiment setup team was evaluated on a series of zeolite adsorption tasks of increasing complexity: single-adsorbate (CH4) and multi-adsorbate (CH4, CO2, CO) adsorption isotherms and heats of adsorption (HOA), across single and multiple zeolite structures. Each task required agents to integrate parameters from multiple source files, assemble force field and adsorbate inputs, and generate RASPA input files. Each simulation setup was repeated five times, and outputs were assessed both by manual inspection and by executing them in RASPA to verify correctness and reproducibility. Success rate (correct configuration for intended task) and execution rate (runs without errors) were measured. Second, the force field retrieval (paper research) team was evaluated by selecting a set of publications and processing each five times to assess reproducibility. Agents extracted force field parameters from the papers, and results were verified for completeness and correctness using Intersection over Union (IoU) as a metric for parameter accuracy. The tested force fields included TraPPE-zeo and EPM2, among others. Additionally, a coordinated experiment was performed in which both teams, overseen by a supervisor agent, were tasked with extracting a force field from a specified publication and using it to set up an adsorption isotherm simulation for a given structure, evaluating end-to-end pipeline integration.
